column8: Planner-owned full, narrowed, and split clustered-handle ranges reach the existing timestamped DAG send boundary with exact immutable evidence; the complete Go cop-client request and error matrix remains open.
Signed clustered-handle boundaries remain ordered and exact while the configured table reader preserves result metadata; missing-handle repair and inconsistent-index recovery remain open.
The bounded direct-table path retains exact physical handle ranges without client-side filtering; index and table consistency checks, repair diagnostics, and index readers remain open.
One nonpartitioned configured table sends normalized clustered-handle ranges through the production-shaped reader; partition selection, random partition readers, and index lookup remain open.
Immutable evidence now includes exact logical bounds and range count beside executor kinds, residual predicate count, and output offsets; index-lookup and back-table runtime statistics remain open.
Clustered access predicates detach while stored-column predicates remain one TiKV Selection condition; partitioned index join, correlated range rebuilding, and index lookup remain open.
Multiple exact handle ranges retain the existing ordered no-paging request authority; paging-size growth, continuation, thresholds, and paged responses remain open.
Nonempty handle ranges continue through the maintained PD and RegionCache route while contradictions avoid PD entirely; adaptive closest-read labels, scope, and replica policy remain open.
The request preserves planner order for full, narrowed, and two-part not-equal ranges and exact encoded bytes; paging continuation, descending scans, and partition range groups remain open.
Every nonempty range plan uses the existing query transport while an empty range plan proves zero sends; multi-region batching, store grouping, concurrency, and fallback remain open.
The bounded range request retains the existing execution-summary envelope and immutable plan evidence; coprocessor-cache admission, keys, hits, and execution-info interaction remain open.
Pure clustered access produces only TableScan while a stored residual preserves TableScan then Selection; index lookup, back-table tasks, and index-side pushdown remain open.
The bounded nonpartitioned reader retains ordered signed ranges and exact residual predicate shape; skewed partition scheduling, lookup merge, and partition result ordering remain open.
